book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Confirmed Stage 3 Breakdown, Overhead Supply & Locked Stop Discipline
question: What do the weekly, daily, and 4-hour charts—alongside post-QIP institutional holdings and insider disposals—tell us about Afcom's Stage 3 breakdown ahead of the November 30 investor call?

epigraph.quote: When both the daily and weekly moving averages roll over into overhead resistance, rallies are for risk reduction—not fresh capital.
epigraph.author: Stage Analysis Desk

web_blocks.html: On November 13, Afcom bounced to ₹1,515.70 on 2.68x volume, splitting `facts_IN` (Stage 3) and TradingView (Stage 2). Two weeks later, the tape broke down cleanly. On the `2026-11-23` NSE/BSE ledger, Afcom fell -9.57% on the week to **₹1,374.90** on light volume (42,960 shares, 0.59x 20-day average) [3]. Price slipped back below both its falling 50-day SMA (₹1,427.16) and 10-week EMA (₹1,413.96) [3]. By the `2026-11-25` live TradingView snapshot, Afcom eased further to **₹1,367.85** (-0.51% 1D, -8.99% 1W, -16.80% 3M, -20.06% off its ₹1,711.00 high) [1, 3].

**Both** trend engines now agree: `facts_IN_2026-11-23.json` and live TradingView (`2026-11-25`) both tag **STAGE_3 (Topping / Pullback)** (`CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT`). Live close ₹1,367.85 sits **-2.51% below the 10-week EMA (₹1,403.01)** and **-3.49% below the 50-day SMA (₹1,417.26)** [3]. It holds only **+3.05% above the 30-week SMA (₹1,327.36)** [3]. Relative strength dropped sharply: 63-day RS vs. Nifty 50 hit **-15.79%** (28-day RS **-21.05%**). Distribution days rose from 4 to **6 in 25 sessions** (`facts_IN_2026-11-23.json`). Note that the scanner's `"Valuation unavailable"` line is a feed placeholder replaced by Chapter 7's Reverse DCF.

web_blocks.takeaway: Both feeds confirm STAGE_3 with 6 distribution days, -15.79% 63-day RS vs. Nifty 50, and an unconfirmed 4H chart (4H RSI 42.72 below 4H EMA20 ₹1,403.25); the ₹1,403–₹1,427 zone is now overhead resistance.

web_blocks.html: The 4-hour chart confirms weak short-term demand. On `options_IN_batch3.json` (`2026-11-25`), Afcom flags `DISLOCATION_AT_MAJOR_SHELF` with `intraday_4h_turn: false`. Four-hour RSI sits at **42.72** (below daily RSI 45.20), and live price ₹1,367.85 stays under 4H EMA20 (₹1,403.25) [3]. Meanwhile, the 50-day SMA fell from ₹1,511.87 twenty-one sessions ago to ₹1,427.16 on the November 23 ledger (`₹1,417.26` live). Any bounce into **₹1,403–₹1,427** now hits trapped buyers from November 13, making rebounds tactical exit zones.

Ownership flows reinforce this overhead supply. May 2026 QIP anchors (Bandhan MF, Abakkus, Ashish Kacholia, Alchemy) lifted DII ownership to 7.61% by September 2026 [12]. Yet Pass 1 uncovered steady insider supply. Promoter-group member Thiagaraja Annamalai sold 51,120 shares for ₹8.41 crore on September 11 and disclosed another sale on November 25 [33]. Co-founder Wg. Cdr. Jaganmohan Manthena resigned on November 12 after his 10.43 lakh share transfer at ₹800 was deferred for lock-in [27, 29]. Also, 1.25 lakh warrants converted on November 12 at ₹863.17 [27]. Against ~41k–43k daily BSE shares, insider supply weighs heavily.

Our **upward-only stop-loss ratchet** protects our 120 Zerodha shares. TradingView's raw model shows a lower stop at ₹1,117.18 and deep support at ₹1,131.34–₹1,165.80 near the 200-day SMA (₹1,163.48). We **never lower a held stop**. Our hard daily-close stop stays locked at **₹1,256.71**—below the 30-week SMA (₹1,327.36) and -8.13% (~1.77x ATR) below ₹1,367.85. Above it, **₹1,310.00–₹1,340.00** is the last weekly floor. Losing ₹1,256.71 opens a drop toward ₹1,163. With Nifty 50 in narrow breadth (48.2% of Nifty 500 > 200-DMA, VIX 17.70) and the H1 call set for **November 30**, capital protection comes first [27].

web_blocks.title: Cash-Equity Only (`NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID`) & Nov 30 Event Gap Risk
paragraphs: Afcom (BSE: 544224) is not in NSE F&O (`NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID`). You cannot buy puts ahead of the November 30 H1 FY27 investor call. On ~41k–43k daily shares and ₹62.77–₹63.68 ATR(14) (~4.6% swing), bad news can gap straight past ₹1,256.71 toward ₹850. Exiting all 120 shares before the call eliminates that unhedgeable gap risk.

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 showed that honest post-lease cash economics cut Afcom's Base Case fair value to ₹1,250 per share—below live prices—Chapter 8 shows why the price tape itself is flashing an urgent warning ahead of the November 30 investor call. Two weeks ago, on November 13, Afcom closed at ₹1,515.70 on heavy volume, creating a temporary disagreement between our two quantitative trend engines. Today, that disagreement is completely gone—and it resolved to the downside.

Let us anchor both dates cleanly. On our November 23, 2026 NSE/BSE market-facts ledger, Afcom dropped 9.57 percent on the week to ₹1,374.90 on thin volume of 42,960 shares. By the live November 25, 2026 TradingView snapshot, it slipped further to ₹1,367.85—down 20.1 percent from its ₹1,711.00 fifty-two-week high. Both our ledger and TradingView now classify Afcom as confirmed Stage 3: Topping and Pullback.

Look at the moving averages underneath that downgrade. Live price at ₹1,367.85 sits 2.51 percent below its 10-week exponential moving average of ₹1,403.01 and 3.49 percent below its 50-day simple moving average of ₹1,417.26. Even more telling, the 50-day moving average has been sliding relentlessly—from ₹1,511.87 twenty-one sessions ago to ₹1,427.16 on the November 23 ledger. Meanwhile, 63-day relative strength against the Nifty 50 plunged to negative 15.79 percent, and distribution days climbed from four to six in twenty-five sessions.

book_subsections.title: Why the 1-Week, 1-Day, and 4-Hour Charts Point to Overhead Supply
paragraphs: Walk down the three timeframes with me. On the weekly chart, Afcom has lost its 10-week EMA and now rests just 3.05 percent above its last major weekly floor—the 30-week simple moving average at ₹1,327.36. On the daily chart, RSI has cooled to 45.20, confirming sellers control momentum. On the 4-hour chart, our options-desk scanner flags a dislocation at a major shelf with no upward turn confirmed: 4-hour RSI sits at 42.72 and price remains trapped below the 4-hour 20-EMA at ₹1,403.25.

What does that mean practically? It means the ₹1,403 to ₹1,427 band—where the 10-week EMA, 4-hour 20-EMA, and falling 50-day moving average converge—has flipped from support into a ceiling of overhead supply. Buyers who chased the November 13 spike near ₹1,515 are now underwater and looking to sell into strength.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.quote: A failed 50-day moving average reclaim followed by six distribution days is the market's way of telling you that supply exceeds demand.
callouts.text: When promoter-group open-market disposals and warrant conversions hit a 41,000-share daily tape, every bounce into ₹1,403–₹1,427 is an opportunity to reduce risk rather than add to a loser.

book_subsections.title: Insider Supply, Thin Liquidity, and Our Locked ₹1,256.71 Hard Stop
paragraphs: The tape weakness makes total sense when you overlay our Pass 1 ownership forensics. While May 2026 QIP institutions like Bandhan Mutual Fund, Abakkus, and Ashish Kacholia still anchor 7.61 percent DII ownership, insider supply has turned negative: promoter-group member Thiagaraja Annamalai sold shares on the open market in September and again in a November 25 disclosure, co-founder Jaganmohan Manthena resigned from the Board and Audit Committee on November 12 after his 10.43 lakh share transfer at ₹800 was deferred for lock-in, and 1.25 lakh warrants converted on November 12 at ₹863.17. On 41,000 to 43,000 shares of daily BSE volume, that supply overhang caps rebounds.

That brings us to our non-negotiable stop-loss discipline. TradingView's automated scanner currently calculates a lower invalidation stop at ₹1,117.18 near the 200-day moving average at ₹1,163.48. We explicitly reject lowering our stop. Under our upward-only ratchet rule for held positions, our hard daily-close stop stays locked at ₹1,256.71—just below the ₹1,327.36 thirty-week moving average and 1.77 times daily ATR below live price. Because Afcom is not in NSE F&O, there are no listed puts to hedge the November 30 investor call, and Nifty 50's narrow breadth—only 48.2 percent of Nifty 500 stocks above their 200-day average with India VIX at 17.70—leaves zero room for complacency.

book_subsections.title: Reading Distribution Days and Narrow Breadth Together
paragraphs: Notice how individual stock distribution interacts with the broader Indian market tape. On the November 23, 2026 ledger, the Nifty 50 sits at 25,349.65 in an uptrend, yet our breadth metrics flash caution: just 55.2 percent of Nifty 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average and only 48.2 percent sit above their 200-day moving average, while India VIX has climbed to 17.70. In narrow-breadth markets, capital concentrates into Stage 2 institutional leaders and abandons Stage 3 mid-caps that print six distribution days in twenty-five sessions.

When daily BSE volume dries down to 41,280 shares—roughly 0.61 times its thirty-day average—while the stock lags the Nifty 50 by 15.79 percent over sixty-three sessions and 21.05 percent over twenty-eight sessions, institutional sponsorship has stepped back to the sidelines. With a daily ATR of ₹62.77 to ₹63.68—roughly 4.6 percent of share price—a negative surprise on November 30 can easily gap straight through ₹1,256.71.

Also notice the key pivot levels mapped on our matrix: Pivot Middle sits at ₹1,348.78, Pivot R1 stands at ₹1,467.42, and Pivot S1 sits way down at ₹1,148.57. That wide ₹200 chasm between the 30-week moving average and Pivot S1 illustrates why holding past ₹1,256.71 invites a swift air-pocket. The tape therefore demands proactive risk reduction into ₹1,403 to ₹1,427 bounces rather than waiting passively for the stop to trigger.

What would it actually take for Afcom to earn back a constructive Stage 2 chart? First, the stock must defend its 30-week moving average at ₹1,327.36 and build a multi-week right-side base on contracting volume, absorbing the promoter-group and warrant-conversion overhang cleanly. Second, price must reclaim both the 10-week EMA and the 50-day moving average on strong volume expansion—turning the falling 50-day slope back upward while reversing its negative 15.79 percent relative-strength lag against the Nifty 50. Until that repair prints on the tape, every rebound stays guilty until proven innocent. Let us now lay out our complete verdict and Zerodha execution plan in Chapter 9.
